explanations.answer: The ways of the kings of Israel
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Jehoram, king of Judah, walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. Ahab was Israel's king (1 Kings 16:29), and Jehoram married one of his daughters. The text puts those two things side by side, and I'll let you do the math.

explanations.answer: The ways of his father Jehoshaphat
explanations.explanation: Close, friend, because Jehoshaphat was Jehoram's father and the king before him. But verse 18 says Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. That's the road the text names.

explanations.answer: The ways of the prophet Elisha
explanations.explanation: Elisha is a prophet (1 Kings 19:16), but he isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses. What verse 18 says is that Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. That's the road he picked. Looking for a prophet in this verse is like looking for a chocolate chip in a plain sugar cookie.

explanations.answer: David had asked Him to spare Judah
explanations.explanation: This passage doesn't say David asked for anything, friend. What it gives is the promise: the LORD had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever (2 Kings 8:19). That's the reason on the page. I'll stick to what's written and not stir in extra ingredients.
